title: Vercel Labs Ships scriptc, a TypeScript-to-Native Compiler That Leaves the JavaScript Engine Behind
gist: Vercel Labs released scriptc, an experimental Apache 2.0 compiler that turns TypeScript into small native executables without Node, V8 or any JavaScript engine, delivering dramatic startup and memory wins over Bun and Node. Early testing shows big throughput and compute penalties, poor coverage of real projects that forces code into an embedded QuickJS fallback, and doubts about longevity given Vercel's abandoned zerolang.

insights.claim: Vercel Labs' scriptc uses the real TypeScript compiler for parsing and type checking, lowers programs to a typed IR, and emits C, LLVM IR, assembly, objects, native executables or WebAssembly (WASI Preview 1), with no Node, V8 or JavaScript engine in the resulting binary.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Signals Vercel exploring TypeScript beyond its runtime/hosting niche into native CLI and edge binaries; watch whether it graduates from Labs.
insights.locator: The repository was created on 22 July 2026

insights.claim: scriptc splits every TypeScript construct into three tiers: compiled statically by default, run dynamically in an embedded ~620KB quickjs-ng engine when --dynamic is passed (for npm packages and any-typed code), or rejected at compile time with an SC error code and a rewrite hint.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The share of code falling into the QuickJS 'island' is the key determinant of real-world performance; ecosystem compatibility is the gating factor.
insights.locator: Every construct lands in one of three tiers

insights.claim: scriptc deliberately diverges from Node semantics: strings are UTF-8, memory is reference counted rather than garbage collected, Object.keys reports declaration order, it requires Node.js 24+ to install, and correctness is enforced by byte-for-byte differential tests of stdout, stderr and exit codes against Node.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Semantic divergences mean scriptc is not a drop-in Node replacement; migration cost stays non-trivial for existing codebases.
insights.locator: The compiler needs Node.js 24 or newer

insights.claim: The scriptc repository, created on 22 July 2026, gathered around 4.9k GitHub stars within roughly two months while remaining explicitly experimental.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Strong developer interest in native-compiled TypeScript; a demand signal for the 'small fast binaries without C/Rust' niche.
insights.locator: The repository was created on 22 July 2026

insights.claim: A benchmark of scriptc 0.0.16 recorded median CLI startup of 1.78ms versus 21.29ms for Bun 1.3.12 and 61.78ms for Node 24.18.0, and idle memory of 1.9MiB for a framework-free node:http server.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Native TypeScript binaries could undercut Bun/Node for CLIs, serverless cold starts and memory-constrained deployments.

insights.claim: When a server uses the Hono framework, scriptc must run 62% of it inside QuickJS via --dynamic, cutting throughput to 18.4k requests per second versus Bun's 70.5k.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: For throughput-bound web servers using real frameworks, JIT runtimes like Bun remain far ahead; scriptc does not threaten them there yet.
insights.quote: Hono required --dynamic, pushing 62% of the server into QuickJS and cutting throughput to 18.4k requests per second against Bun's 70.5k
insights.locator: The same tests found Hono required --dynamic

insights.claim: A Hacker News tester found scriptc about 7.5x slower than Node 24 on a byte-array workload, but with 12x faster startup (1.5ms vs 18.6ms), 72x less memory (2.5MiB vs 181MiB) and a single 370KB dependency-free executable.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The trade-off profile favors short-lived, footprint-sensitive workloads over compute-heavy ones.
insights.quote: scriptc is about 7.5x slower than Node 24, even after Claude tried making some scriptc-specific optimizations
insights.locator: On Hacker News, one developer reported

insights.claim: An attempt by Remo Jansen to compile the TypeScript 6 compiler with scriptc failed on an internal compiler error; separately he measured a 3.6ms cold start versus Node's 48.9ms but a much slower 2.33s on compute.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Large real-world codebases do not yet compile; maturity is well short of production.
insights.locator: Remo Jansen's attempt to compile the TypeScript 6 compiler

insights.claim: Filip Pizlo argued scriptc's choice of floats for all numbers with deferred integer inference skips half the problem of fast JavaScript, and that falling back to QuickJS is a poor fit for a performance project because any-typed code is common enough that real programs will keep landing in the slow path.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Structural design limits suggest performance gaps versus JIT engines may persist, not just reflect early-version immaturity.
insights.quote: half the problem of fast JS
insights.locator: Filip Pizlo argued that using floats

insights.claim: One developer reported that scriptc's coverage check produced hundreds of errors on every local project tried, arguing that if code must be written from scratch without third-party libraries, purpose-built compiled languages like Rust, Go or Zig are better choices.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Adoption hinges on npm ecosystem compatibility; without it, scriptc competes poorly with established native languages.
insights.quote: For every single of them the coverage generates hundreds of errors and so it is basically useless.
insights.locator: One developer found coverage produced hundreds of errors

insights.claim: Commenters doubt scriptc's longevity, pointing to Vercel's zerolang project, which stopped receiving commits weeks after launch.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Vercel Labs experiments carry abandonment risk; teams should avoid building dependencies on them until sustained maintenance is evident.

themes.theme: AI agents and the value case

insights.claim: Simon Willison noted coding agents landed 918,000 lines in a single week (in the context of scriptc's rapid development), while calling small fast binaries without writing C or Rust a valuable capability.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Agent-driven development is enabling very rapid build-out of ambitious compiler projects, but raises questions about maintainability and depth of design.
